speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any feeding difficulties, temperature instability, or a specific odor on your skin or urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis (likely Group B Streptococcus or E. coli) secondary to chorioamnionitis and prematurity.
I see from your history that you were born small for gestational age at 31 weeks with low Apgar scores and a history of chorioamnionitis. Given your increasing lethargy and tonic seizure, I need to confirm metabolic derangements and infection sources. REQUEST TEST: Blood culture, CBC with differential, Blood glucose, Electrolytes, Serum ammonia, and Lactate.
